newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander says new buys boost 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: Santander says new buys boost 1996 results.

text.p: Spain's Banco Santander said on Tuesday its 1996 results saw key positive contributions from new acquisitions.
"We have intensified the strategy of diversifying into new markets," chairman Emilio Botin said in statement accompanying the results.
Key purchases in 1996 included a $495-million buy of Chile's Banco Osorno y La Union and $280-million investment in Banco Central Hispano Puerto Rico, as well as buys in Peru and Germany.
These contributed to a 29.6 percent rise in goodwill amortisation, the bank said.
Acquistions made in the final quarter of 1996 will be consolidated in 1997.

Banco Santander said earlier on Tuesday 1996 net attributable profit rose to 85.60 billion pesetas from 75.39 billion pesetas. Net profit rose to 120.53 billion from 101.87 billion while pre-tax profit rose to 163.19 billion from 146.00 bilion pesetas.
